title: An Autopsy of a Digital Mind

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The chapter's range makes comparison more revealing than collecting isolated quotations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Judgment returns through the authority that an explanation acquires over ordinary choices.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book's four experiments begin to speak across their apparent boundaries.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The fourth experiment carries judgment into law, rights, and public institutions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks how fallible people can exercise power over other lives.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Appeal, remedies, and responsibility matter alongside the language of fairness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its machine-justice sections examine automated decisions without assuming hatred is required.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The text offers philosophical arguments rather than a complete legal treatise.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The earlier inner court now meets institutions that can enforce their judgments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That structure gives the collection a larger question than any single aphorism.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The preface explicitly says that this volume lacks completed systematic validation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its claims include metaphors, hypotheses, generalizations, and judgments requiring different scrutiny.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Feeling recognized cannot by itself distinguish them or establish their truth.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed future validation work would preserve evidence, exceptions, and uncertainty.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That work remains a research direction, not an accomplished guarantee.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book also refuses therapeutic, clinical, and legal authority.
